title: [HOLD for grain refactor] hub/cujtest, interop: run the 12 Grain Hub CUJs against real bwsalmon/grain instances
body:
**HOLD UNTIL `bwsalmon/grain` REFACTORING LANDS:** Once `bwsalmon/grain` has been updated to speak the new Grain Hub Grainfile subscription, notification, and same-repo content proxy protocol, replace the simulated/fake Grain driver in the 12 CUJ suite (`hub/cujtest`) and `scripts/grain-interop.sh` (`.grain/workflows/grain-interop.yml`) with real `bwsalmon/grain` daemon instances:

### 1. Plug real `bwsalmon/grain` instances into `hub/cujtest` (`docs/cujs.md` CUJ-01 through CUJ-12)
- Implement the `GrainNodeDriver` in `hub/cujtest` backed by real `cmd/grain` daemon instances built from `bwsalmon/grain` (running against local git repos and the GitHub simulator).
- Run all 12 Critical User Journeys (`CUJ-01` through `CUJ-12`) end-to-end with real Grain daemons subscribing to `recipient` URLs, receiving `grainfile_event` notifications over `rendezvous`, fetching `.task.grain.md` / `.process.grain.md` files and authorized same-repo `references` via `/v1/grainfiles/content`, executing tasks/processes, reporting `depends_on` completions, and serving tunneled local UIs (`hub/nodeui`).

### 2. Update `scripts/grain-interop.sh` and `hub/conformance`
- Update `scripts/grain-interop.sh` (`.grain/workflows/grain-interop.yml`) and `silo conformance` (`hub/conformance`) to verify the Grainfile subscription, trigger, and same-repo content proxy flows against real `bwsalmon/grain`.
- Record the real-Grain CUJ test run report under `docs/test-runs/`.

title: [HOLD for grain refactor] pkg/orchestrator, pkg/tunnel, pkg/ui: support persistent sandboxes with auto-restart and host-port / UI sub-path routing
body:
**HOLD UNTIL `bwsalmon/grain` REFACTORING LANDS.**

Implement **Persistent Sandboxes / Staging Environments** in `bwsalmon/grain` (`pkg/orchestrator`, `pkg/staterepo`, `pkg/model`, `pkg/tunnel`, `pkg/ui`, `ui/`) so a Grain deployment can run standing staging environments and long-lived services inside managed sandboxes:

### 1. Persistent Sandbox Specification & State (`pkg/model`, `pkg/staterepo`, `pkg/repodecl`)
- Allow defining persistent sandboxes in the deployment state (`tables/persistent_sandboxes.json`) and/or repository declarations:
  - **Repository & ref:** Target repository (`owner/name`) and branch/ref (cloned into the sandbox workspace on startup, with optional auto-update/fetch on restart).
  - **Predefined startup command (`command`):** The shell command executed inside the sandbox workspace once the repository is checked out.
  - **Resources & capabilities:** VM sizing (`cpus`, `memory_mb`, `disk_gb`), network access, and attached capabilities/secrets.
  - **Exposure mode:**
    - **Host port binding (`host_port` -> `sandbox_port`):** Bind a port on the Grain host and forward TCP/HTTP traffic through Grain to the sandbox's listening port, OR
    - **Grain UI sub-path (`ui_subpath`, e.g. `/staging/<name>` -> `sandbox_port`):** Expose an HTTP service inside the sandbox under a sub-path of the Grain UI.

### 2. Supervised Lifecycle & Automatic Restart (`pkg/orchestrator`, `pkg/daemon`)
- **Start on deployment startup:** When the Grain daemon starts (including after a deployment restart or upgrade), reconcile all enabled persistent sandboxes and boot/start them automatically.
- **Restart on command or VM exit:** Supervise the predefined command and sandbox VM continuously:
  - If the predefined command exits (whether cleanly or with a non-zero exit code) or the underlying sandbox VM terminates unexpectedly, automatically restart it (with bounded exponential backoff on rapid crash loops, resetting backoff after sustained uptime) and record exit events and live stdout/stderr ring-buffer logs.
  - Ensure persistent sandboxes do not consume the task-runner concurrency slots (`max_concurrent_runs`) used for normal task attempts, or account for their VM resources explicitly in `read_deployment_health`.

### 3. Host-Port Forwarding & Grain UI Sub-Path HTTP Reverse Proxy (`pkg/tunnel`, `pkg/ui`)
- **Host port binding (via Grain):**
  - Open a listener on the configured host port (validating no collision with Grain's own ports or other persistent sandboxes) and proxy connections into the sandbox's target port across restarts.
- **Grain UI sub-path reverse proxy (`/staging/<name>/...`):**
  - Mount an HTTP reverse proxy (supporting HTTP/1.1, SSE streaming, and WebSocket `101` upgrades) under the Grain UI mux (e.g. `/staging/<name>/...`), stripping/rewriting the prefix as configured.
  - Because it is served under `pkg/ui`, the staging environment is automatically reachable locally, through `grain-relay`, and through the Grain Hub's `hub/nodeui` reverse tunnel (`https://<node>.<node-ui-domain>/staging/<name>/...`), inheriting the deployment's authentication and role-based access control.

### 4. Grain UI Management View (`pkg/ui`, `ui/`)
- Add a **Persistent Sandboxes / Staging** view (or section in Sandboxes) in the Grain UI showing each persistent sandbox's state (`starting`, `running`, `restarting`, `stopped`), repository/branch, command, uptime, restart count, bound host port or clickable `/staging/<name>/` UI link, live stdout/stderr log tail, and controls to **Restart**, **Stop/Start**, or **Rebuild Sandbox** (fresh VM + fresh clone).

### Verification
- Add unit and integration tests covering persistent sandbox creation, automatic restart when the predefined command exits, automatic startup when the Grain daemon restarts, host-port forwarding, and HTTP/WebSocket proxying under a Grain UI sub-path.

title: [HOLD for grain refactor] pkg/hubnode, pkg/ui, ui: implement 5-role via.Hub UI permissions, resolved light/dark theme, U3/U5/U7, and G1-G4 nodeui
body:
**HOLD UNTIL `bwsalmon/grain` REFACTORING LANDS.**

Update `bwsalmon/grain` (`pkg/hubnode`, `pkg/ui`, `pkg/access`, `ui/`) so that when a user switches into a deployment's single-tenant Grain UI from the Grain Hub (`bwsalmon/silo` `hub/nodeui`), the deployment serves its full single-tenant Grain UI with the **exact permissions accorded to the user's Hub role (`owner`, `admin`, `member`, `proposer`, `viewer`)** and the **user's Hub-resolved `light` / `dark` theme**, and supports `U3`, `U5`, `U7`, and `G1–G4`:

### 1. Answer `http` Streams & `via.Hub` Identity/Role/Theme Context (`pkg/hubnode`, `pkg/ui`, `G1–G2`)
- Announce `ui: {"offered": true, "team": "<team>", "access": "..."}` in the Hub rendezvous `hello` message when configured with a Hub.
- Accept `http` streams opened by `hub/nodeui` (`{"type":"http","node":"...","viewer":"...","role":"owner|admin|member|proposer|viewer","team":"...","require_approval":true|false,"theme":"light|dark","request_id":"..."}`), answer `{"type":"ok","access":"..."}`, and serve the proxied HTTP/1.1 request (including SSE and WebSocket upgrades) in-process with a `via.Hub` context mark (`isLoopbackRequest` must return `false`).
- Accept `<node>.<node-ui-domain>` in the Host guard for `via.Hub` requests.

### 2. 5-Role Permission Enforcement in `pkg/ui` & `ui/` (`G3`)
- Map the Hub-claimed `role` (`owner`, `admin`/`team-admin`, `member`, `proposer`, `viewer`) and `require_approval` policy to concrete permissions enforced by an outer middleware on `pkg/ui`'s mux (and surfaced on `/api/me` so the SPA hides disallowed controls cosmetically):
  1. **`owner` and `admin` (`team-admin`):** Full deployment UI access (settings, secrets, capabilities, persistent/ephemeral sandboxes, approve/reject/cancel/requeue tasks, file tasks, and chat with the deployment's standing Director or interactive task sessions). If the deployment owner explicitly configured `hub_ui: read-only` to cap non-owner access, honor that cap.
  2. **`member`:** Full task & interactive session workflow (view all tasks/runs/transcripts/metrics, file tasks, chat with the deployment's Director or interactive sessions, reply to `ask_question` / `approval_request`, cancel/requeue tasks, and approve/reject `proposed` tasks except self-approval; when `require_approval: true`, newly filed tasks land in state `proposed` awaiting another `member`/`admin`'s approval), while deployment-admin settings/secrets/capability mutations return `403 Forbidden`.
  3. **`proposer`:** Read access (`GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS` on safe routes) plus permission to submit/propose tasks (`POST /api/tasks`, which always land in state `proposed` awaiting approval from a `member`/`admin`); all other state-mutating requests (approving/canceling tasks, posting to existing sessions, changing settings/secrets) return `403 Forbidden`.
  4. **`viewer`:** Strictly read-only (`GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS` on safe routes; all `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` requests and any `GET` route returning secrets/credentials/tokens return `403 Forbidden`).
- Add a route-classification test that walks every registered route in `pkg/ui` and verifies that no unclassified route or credential-returning `GET` is accessible to `viewer`/`proposer` over `via.Hub`.
- Log structured audit entries (`request_id`, `viewer`, `role`, `team`, and any `403` role refusal).

### 3. Hub-Resolved `light` / `dark` Theme Propagation (`pkg/ui`, `ui/src/ThemeModeContext.jsx`, `ui/src/AppThemeProvider.jsx`)
- Expose the Hub-passed `theme` (`"light"` or `"dark"`, from `nodeui.Message.Theme` / `X-Grain-Hub-UI-Theme`) on `/api/me` for `via.Hub` requests.
- In `ui/src/ThemeModeContext.jsx` / `ui/src/AppThemeProvider.jsx`, when the SPA is served via the Hub with a Hub-resolved `theme` (`"light"` or `"dark"`), apply that theme directly so switching deployments in the Hub preserves the user's exact `light` / `dark` / `auto` appearance across every deployment origin without requiring per-origin `localStorage` toggling.

### 4. `U3` (In-Run Approvals), `U5` (Hub Task Link), `U7` (Interactive Sessions), & `G4` (Retire Relay for UI)
- **`U3`:** Emit `approval_request` events over the Hub event stream when a run blocks on a human approval/question and resume when `tasks.TypeApprove` arrives.
- **`U5`:** Display the Hub task link (`<hub>/tasks/<id>`) on tasks dispatched or mirrored to the Hub.
- **`U7`:** Advertise `FeatureInteractive`, stream `awaiting_reply` and `message` events to the Hub, and deliver human replies from the Hub into the live session.
- **`G4`:** Stop dialing `grain-relay` for UI traffic when a Hub is configured and no remote executors require the relay.

### Verification
- Run `go test -race ./pkg/hubnode/... ./pkg/ui/...` and `npm test` in `ui/`.

title: [HOLD for grain refactor] pkg/hubnode, pkg/orchestrator: consume Grainfile v1 (.task.grain.md, .process.grain.md, and .jinja2 templates) over Hub rendezvous
body:
**HOLD UNTIL `bwsalmon/grain` REFACTORING LANDS.**

Implement **Grainfile `v1` (`.task.grain.md`, `.process.grain.md`, `.task.grain.md.jinja2`, and `.process.grain.md.jinja2`) subscription, consumption, and execution** in `bwsalmon/grain` (`pkg/hubnode`, `pkg/orchestrator`, `pkg/model`):

### 1. Subscriptions & Event Catch-Up (`pkg/hubnode`)
- Allow a Grain deployment to declare its `recipient` URL(s) and its subscribed repositories, folders, and `.process.grain.md` / `.process.grain.md.jinja2` URLs in the Hub rendezvous `hello` / `subscribe` protocol, persisting the last processed `grainfile_event` cursor in deployment state and sending `catchup` on reconnect.
- Handle all Grainfile event types from the Hub:
  - `task_ready`: Enqueue an idempotent task keyed by `(grainfile_url)` (or `(grainfile_url, commit)` when updated before execution), respecting `requestor` and `depends_on`.
  - `task_removed`: Cancel any queued or running task originated from the removed or re-drafted `.task.grain.md`.
  - `process_updated` / `process_removed`: Register, update, or remove standing process definitions (including local cron/schedule triggers when `when.schedule` is used).
  - `process_triggered`: Enqueue a process run for the triggering webhook/event delivery (`delivery_id` idempotency, passing event variables and honoring `gate: true` by posting a commit status / check run).
  - `dependency_completed`: Unblock waiting `.task.grain.md` items whose `depends_on` upstream tasks have completed.

### 2. Commit-Pinned Content & Same-Repo Reference Fetching (`pkg/hubnode`, `pkg/orchestrator`)
- Fetch the Grainfile markdown body and any authorized same-repo `references` (both individual files and folder/tree references) at the exact indexed `commit_sha` via `/v1/grainfiles/content` or the Hub rendezvous mux stream (`fetch_grainfile` / `fetch_reference`), placing fetched reference files into the sandbox workspace (e.g. `.grain/references/...`) for the agent run.

### 3. `.task.grain.md.jinja2` & `.process.grain.md.jinja2` Template Consumption
- Support consuming parameterized `.task.grain.md.jinja2` and `.process.grain.md.jinja2` templates from the Hub, passing deployment-configured or trigger-supplied template variables (`?var.<name>=<value>`) and validating the rendered `.task.grain.md` / `.process.grain.md` before execution.

### 4. Completion Reporting for Cross-Deployment `depends_on`
- When a `.task.grain.md` run finishes, send `grainfile_completed` (and stream the terminal `result` event over `hub/live`) so the Hub marks the Grainfile completed and unblocks any downstream `.task.grain.md` (on this or another deployment) that `depends_on` it.

### Verification
- Add end-to-end tests in `pkg/hubnode` and `pkg/orchestrator` against the `bwsalmon/silo` Hubserver and run `go test -race ./pkg/...`.

title: [HOLD for grain refactor] pkg/orchestrator, pkg/mcp: add pre-warmed sandbox pool and per-(repo, base_SHA) base_branch_status caching
body:
**HOLD UNTIL `bwsalmon/grain` REFACTORING LANDS.**

Implement the two highest-leverage infrastructure throughput and latency optimizations identified from this deployment's `grain metrics` measurements (`pkg/orchestrator`, `pkg/mcp`):

### 1. Pre-Warmed Sandbox Pool (`pkg/orchestrator`)
- **Problem:** Cold sandbox VM creation and boot currently averages ~52s (`p50 38s`, `p90 1m09s`) before the first agent turn can start.
- **Solution:** Maintain a configurable pool of `1–2` pre-warmed idle sandboxes (`max_idle_pool`, default `1`) with the base VM image already booted and ready. When a task is dispatched, claim a pre-warmed sandbox from the pool, clone the target repository/branch, and replenish the idle pool in the background, cutting dispatch-to-first-turn latency from ~52s to `<5s`.

### 2. Per-`(repo, base_branch, head_sha)` Caching for `base_branch_status` (`pkg/mcp`, `pkg/github`)
- **Problem:** `base_branch_status` currently averages `5.8s` per call (`max 55.8s`) because each call queries GitHub check-runs and tail logs for the base branch from scratch.
- **Solution:** Cache the result of `base_branch_status` in the controller keyed by `(repo, base_branch, head_sha)` with a short TTL (`60–120s`, invalidated when a new commit lands on the base branch) so concurrent runs checking the same base branch SHA receive an instant response without redundant GitHub API calls.

### Verification
- Add unit tests for the pre-warmed sandbox pool lifecycle (claim, replenish, shutdown cleanup) and `base_branch_status` cache hit/invalidation, and run `go test -race ./pkg/...`.

title: [HOLD for grain refactor] pkg/agent, pkg/capability: add sandbox_T (2h/4h) deadline capability and prompt guidance for wait_for_checks and read_file
body:
**HOLD UNTIL `bwsalmon/grain` REFACTORING LANDS.**

Implement the agent prompt efficiency improvements and the configurable extended sandbox deadline capability (`sandbox_T`) in `bwsalmon/grain` (`pkg/agent`, `pkg/capability`, `pkg/orchestrator`):

### 1. Extended Run Deadline Capability (`sandbox_T`: `2h` / `4h`) (`pkg/capability`, `pkg/orchestrator`)
- Add a parameterized or tiered run-timeout capability (e.g. `sandbox-2h` and `sandbox-4h`, or `sandbox_timeout`) that tasks can request via `capabilities` in `propose_task` / UI task creation when running long E2E, `kind` cluster, or fault-injection test suites that exceed the default run deadline.

### 2. Base Agent Prompt Guidelines for `wait_for_checks` and `read_file` Chunking (`pkg/agent`)
- Update the base system prompt assembled for sandbox runs based on `grain metrics` findings:
  1. **Use `wait_for_checks` instead of polling `pull_request_status`:** Instruct agents to call `wait_for_checks` once after `git push` (which blocks until CI finishes or fails and credits wait time back to the run budget) rather than calling `pull_request_status` repeatedly in a polling loop.
  2. **Targeted `read_file(offset, limit)` windows:** Instruct agents to pass `offset` and `limit` (e.g. 200–300 lines) when reading large source files so tool outputs stay under the 16 KB truncation cap (`12.2%` of `read_file` calls were previously truncated).
  3. **Verify target paths before `edit_file`:** Remind agents to read the exact target lines immediately before `edit_file` to avoid stale-context mismatches (`13.0%` error rate on `edit_file`).

### Verification
- Add unit tests for the `sandbox_T` deadline override and prompt assembly in `pkg/capability`, `pkg/orchestrator`, and `pkg/agent`, and run `go test -race ./pkg/...`.

title: [HOLD for grain refactor] pkg/hubnode, pkg/agent: support multi-user Hub shared chat sessions and Google Chat-linked rooms
body:
Update `bwsalmon/grain` (`pkg/hubnode`, `pkg/agent`, `pkg/orchestrator`) after the refactor so a Grain deployment connected to the Hub can serve as the backing agent (or `@mentioned` secondary agent) for **Hub Shared Chat Sessions** and **Google Chat-linked rooms** (building on Task #119):

1. **Multi-User Transcript & Attribution (`pkg/hubnode`, `pkg/agent`):**
   - When receiving `tasks.TypeMessage` batches on an interactive session stream from the Hub (`hub/chats`), format each human participant's message with their verified identity and source (`[alice@example.com]: ...` or `[bob@example.com via Google Chat]: ...`) in the agent's conversation history so the agent knows who is speaking in a group room of engineers, PMs, or operators.
2. **`@mention` vs. `All messages` Turn-Taking & Cross-Deployment Proposals:**
   - Support the Hub shared chat session's wakeup semantics (only running an agent turn when the Hub dispatches a turn trigger, while keeping passive room messages in context).
   - When the agent in a shared chat calls `propose_task` (or generates `.task.grain.md` files), allow targeting any deployment in the Hub via its canonical URL (`recipient: https://<hub-host>/deployments/<name>`) and link the proposed task back to the Hub shared chat session.

### Verification
- Run `go test -race ./pkg/hubnode/... ./pkg/agent/...`.

title: [HOLD for grain refactor] repo: merge bwsalmon/silo into bwsalmon/grain as a single Go module preserving git history
body:
Merge `bwsalmon/silo` (Grain Hub, Grainfile `v1` specification/linter/schemas, TypeScript SDK, and Hub UI) into `bwsalmon/grain` as a single repository and single Go module (`module github.com/bwsalmon/grain`) while preserving full `git log` / `git blame` history from both repositories:

### 1. Target Unified Directory Layout in `bwsalmon/grain`
- **Single Go module (`go.mod` at root: `module github.com/bwsalmon/grain`):**
  - Remove the external `github.com/bwsalmon/silo` dependency from `go.mod`; `pkg/hubnode`, `pkg/daemon`, and `hub/...` live in the same Go module and compile/test together atomically.
- **Directory mapping from `bwsalmon/silo` into `bwsalmon/grain`:**
  - `hub/` -> `hub/` (all Hub packages: `hub/server`, `hub/directory`, `hub/tasks`, `hub/live`, `hub/nodeui`, `hub/grainfiles`, `hub/chats`, `hub/gchat`, `hub/rendezvous`, `hub/registry`, `hub/identity`, `hub/claims`, `hub/lease`, `hub/conformance`, `hub/cujtest`, `hub/faulttest`, `hub/security`, etc.)
  - `events/` -> `events/`
  - `internal/fakegrain/` (and other `silo/internal/*` packages) -> `internal/fakegrain/` (or `hub/internal/...`)
  - `cmd/silo/` -> `cmd/silo/` (and also wire `grain hub serve` / `grain hub migrate` / `grain hub token` subcommands into `cmd/grain/`)
  - `ui/` (from `silo`) -> `ui-hub/` (or `hub/ui/web/`, updating `hub/ui` build/embed scripts and `Dockerfile.hub` while keeping `bwsalmon/grain`'s `ui/` at root)
  - `sdk/ts/` -> `sdk/ts/`
  - `schemas/grainfiles/` -> `schemas/grainfiles/`
  - `tools/grainfiles/` -> `tools/grainfiles/`
  - `examples/grainfiles/` -> `examples/grainfiles/`
  - `deploy/` (from `silo`: `k8s/`, `terraform/`) -> `deploy/hub/`
  - `Dockerfile` (from `silo`) -> `Dockerfile.hub`
  - `docs/grainfile-v1.md`, `docs/grainfiles-spec.md`, `docs/grainfiles.md`, `docs/cujs.md` -> `docs/`, and remaining Hub docs -> `docs/hub/`
  - **Drop `old/`** from `silo` before merging so legacy pre-Hub code is not carried into the open-source repository.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Merge Procedure (Preserving Git History)
1. Fetch `bwsalmon/silo` `main` (`http://192.168.9.1:9728/bwsalmon/silo.git` / `https://github.com/bwsalmon/silo.git`) into a temporary staging branch.
2. In the staging branch of `silo`:
   - `git rm -rf old/`
   - `git mv` the overlapping top-level paths (`ui/` -> `ui-hub/`, `deploy/` -> `deploy/hub/`, `Dockerfile` -> `Dockerfile.hub`, and Hub-specific docs into `docs/hub/`).
   - Rewrite Go imports and module references from `github.com/bwsalmon/silo` to `github.com/bwsalmon/grain` across all `.go` files.
3. Merge the prepared `silo` branch into `bwsalmon/grain` with `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories` (preserving full commit history and `git blame` across both trees).
4. Rewrite `github.com/bwsalmon/silo/...` imports in `pkg/hubnode/`, `pkg/daemon/`, and `pkg/policy/` to `github.com/bwsalmon/grain/...`, remove `github.com/bwsalmon/silo` from `go.mod`, and run `go mod tidy`.
5. Unify `.grain/workflows/tests.yml` (and `Makefile`) so the CI pipeline runs both the Grain daemon/node test suites and the Hub (`hub`, `grainfiles`, `sdk`, `ui-hub`, `ui-hub e2e`, `manifests`, `terraform`, `kind`) jobs in one repository.

### Verification
- Run `go test -race ./hub/... ./pkg/hubnode/... ./pkg/daemon/...`, `python3 tools/grainfiles/grainlint.py --self-test`, `python3 tools/grainfiles/grainlint.py examples/grainfiles`, and `npm test` in `sdk/ts`, `ui/`, and `ui-hub/`.

title: Standardize all timestamps across Grain to RFC 3339
body:
Standardize all timestamp inputs, parsers, schemas, and documentation across `bwsalmon/grain` in its entirety to **RFC 3339** (`time.RFC3339` / `time.RFC3339Nano`), removing ad-hoc date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and multi-layout timestamp amalgams:

## Required Changes

1. **`not_before` on Tasks, Proposals, UI/API, and CLI (`pkg/mcp/`, `pkg/orchestrator/`, `pkg/ui/`, `pkg/cli/`):**
   - Update `mcp.ParseNotBefore` in `pkg/mcp/mock_tools.go` (and its schema/description on `propose_task`, plus `pkg/orchestrator/finish.go`, `pkg/ui/`, and `pkg/cli/`) to accept strictly **RFC 3339 timestamps** (`time.RFC3339`, e.g. `2026-10-14T09:00:00Z`), removing the bare `YYYY-MM-DD` (`2006-01-02`) fallback.
   - Update tests (`pkg/mcp/live_proposal_test.go`, `pkg/daemon/proposal_not_before_test.go`, `pkg/orchestrator/finish_test.go`, `pkg/ui/task_not_before_test.go`, etc.) to pass RFC 3339 timestamps.

2. **`read_grain_metrics` and CLI/API Window Bounds (`since` / `until`):**
   - Update `since` and `until` parsing and tool schema descriptions in `pkg/capability/selfdebug/` and `pkg/cli/` (e.g. `grain metrics`) so `since` and `until` take strictly **RFC 3339 timestamps** (matching `read_grain_log` in `pkg/capability/grainlog/grainlog.go`), removing bare `2006-01-02` date parsing.

3. **CI & Task Filter Timestamp Parsing (`pkg/ci/filter.go`, `pkg/cli/taskfilters.go`, `pkg/cli/list.go`):**
   - Replace multi-layout timestamp loops (`[]string{time.RFC3339, "2006-01-02T15:04:05", "2006-01-02 15:04", "2006-01-02"}` in `pkg/ci/filter.go` and bare date parsing in `pkg/cli/taskfilters.go` / `pkg/cli/list.go`) with standard RFC 3339 timestamp parsing (`time.RFC3339`).
   - Keep custom field type `date` (`CustomFieldDateLayout` in `pkg/model/custom_field.go`) only if explicitly representing a calendar-date custom field, or migrate if appropriate; ensure all point-in-time timestamps across Grain use RFC 3339.

## Verification
- Run `go test ./...` across `bwsalmon/grain`.
